The fix is done.

## What was wrong

In `combineConfigs` (`src/util/config/load.ts`), the dedup logic uses a `seenProviders` Set keyed by `providerDedupeKey(provider)`. The caller treats a key of `undefined` as "never seen — always push":

```ts
const key = providerDedupeKey(provider);
if (key === undefined) {
  providers.push(provider);   // no dedup at all
  return;
}
if (!seenProviders.has(key)) { ... }
```

But `providerDedupeKey` returned `undefined` precisely for **ApiProvider instances** and **objects with function-valued properties** (since those can't be JSON-serialized). That meant the same repeated reference was blindly appended every time → duplicates.

## The fix

For those two cases, return the provider **reference itself** as the key instead of `undefined`. Since the `Set` compares objects by identity:

- **Same object/instance repeated** → same key → collapsed to one entry ✓
- **Distinct references** (even structurally identical, even same class) → different keys → each preserved ✓

Strings and functions were already keyed by identity/value, and plain serializable objects still dedup structurally via `JSON.stringify` (unchanged existing behavior). I also changed the `JSON.stringify` `catch` fallback from `undefined` to `provider` so any unexpectedly-unserializable object still dedups by reference rather than duplicating.

No test files were touched.
